questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The product of electrolysis of aqueous NaCl solution on anode and cathode respectively is
questions.solution:
In case of electrolysis of aqueous NaCl , oxidation and reduction reaction occurs at anode and cathode respectively as shown below:
At cathode
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})+\mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{OH}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})$
At anode
$\mathrm{Cl}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) \longrightarrow \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{e}^{-}$
Net cell reaction is as follows
$\mathrm{NaCl}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{OH}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{~g})$
Thus, the product of electrolysis of NaCl solution on cathode and anode is $\mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{Cl}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the correct statement from the following.
options: The greater positive value of $E_{\mathrm{OP}}^{\circ}$ indicates greater reactivity of metal
$\mathrm{F}^{-}$is strong oxidant whileCu2+ ${ }^{2+}$ is weak reductant
The metals placed above Mg in the electrochemical series do not decompose water at ordinary temperature
Oxides of Hg do not decompose on heating
questions.solution:
According to the applications of electrochemical series on moving from top to bottom in electrochemical series, the values of $E_{\mathrm{oP}}^{\circ}$ of metals decrease, and thus reactivity of metals of $E_{\mathrm{op}}^{\circ}$ indicates greater reactivity of metal. On the other hand, $\mathrm{F}^{-}$is poor reductant while $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ is strong oxidant.
The metals placed above Mg in ECS decompose water at ordinary temperature to liberate $\mathrm{H}_2$. Oxides of Hg decomposes on heating.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A student made the following observations in the laboratory.
I. Clean copper metal did not react with 1 molar $\mathrm{Pb}\left(\mathrm{NO}_3\right)_2$ solution
II. Clean lead metal dissolved in a 1 molar $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ solution and crystals of Ag metal appeared
III. Clean silver metal did not react with 1 molar $\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{NO}_3\right)_2$ solution
The order of decrease in reducing character of three metals is
questions.solution:
Metal placed above in electrochemical series replaces the other from its salt solution which is lower in the series.
The low $E^{\circ}$ value containing metals have the high reducing character.
Thus, order of reducing character of three metals is
$\mathrm{Pb}\gt\mathrm{Cu}\gt\mathrm{Ag}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The conductivity of $0.001028 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$ acetic acid is $4.95 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}$. Find out its dissociation constant if $\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}$ for acetic acid is $390.5 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{K}{C} & =\frac{4.95 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}}{0.001028 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}} \times \frac{1000 \mathrm{~cm}^3}{\mathrm{~L}} \\ & =48.15 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\ \alpha & =\frac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ}}=\frac{48.15}{390.5}=0.1233 \\ K & =\frac{C \alpha^2}{(1-\alpha)}=\frac{0.001028 \times(0.1233)^2}{(1-0.1233)} \\ & =1.78 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct?
options: $E_{\text {cell }}$ and $\Delta_t G$ of cell reaction both are extensive properties.
$E_{\text {cell }}$ and $\Delta_r G$ of cell reaction both are intensive properties.
$E_{\text {cell }}$ in the intensive property while $\Delta_r G$ of cell reaction is an extensive property.
$E_{\text {cell }}$ is an extensive property while $\Delta_r G$ of cell reaction is an intensive property.
questions.solution: $E_{\text {cell }}$ is intensive while $\Delta_r G$ is extensive. (In the relation, $\Delta G=-n F E, E$ depends only on the nature of the cell reaction so it is intensive whereas value of $\Delta G$ depends upon the value of $n$. So it is extensive.)

$\begin{aligned} & E_y^{\circ}=-1.2 \mathrm{~V} \\ & E_x^{\circ}=+0.5 \mathrm{~V} \\ & E_z^{\circ}=-3.0 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}\because$ Higher the reduction potential, lesser the reducing power.
$\therefore$ Order of reducing power is $Z \gt X \gt Y$

questions.q:
What is the electrode potential (in V ) of the following electrode at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ?
$\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}(0.1 \mathrm{M}) \mid \mathrm{Ni}(s)$
(Standard reaction potential of $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+} \mid \mathrm{Ni}$ is $-0.25 \mathrm{~V}, \frac{2.303 R T}{F}=0.06$ )
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} E_{\text {cell }}^{\circ} & =E_{\text {cell }}^{\circ}-\frac{2.303 R T}{n F} \log \left[\frac{[\mathrm{Ni}]}{\left[\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}\right]}\right] \\ & =-0.25-\frac{0.06}{2} \log \left(\frac{1}{0.1}\right) \quad(\because n=2) \\ & =-0.25-0.03 \times 1 \\ E_{\text {cell }} & =-0.28 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: 4.5 g of aluminium (Atomic mass 27 amu) is deposited at cathode from $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ solution by a certain quantity of electric charge. The volume of hydrogen produced at STP from $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions in solution by the same quantity of electric charge will be
questions.solution:
From second law of Faraday
$\frac{m_{\mathrm{Al}}}{m_{\mathrm{H}}}=\frac{E_{\mathrm{Al}}}{E_{\mathrm{H}}}\therefore \frac{4.5}{m_{\mathrm{H}}}=\frac{27 / 3}{1}$
or $m_{\mathrm{H}}=0.5 \mathrm{~g}\because 2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{H}_2$ volume at $\mathrm{STP}=22.4 \mathrm{~L}\therefore 0.5 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{H}_2$ volume at STP
$=\frac{22.4 \times 0.5}{2} \mathrm{~L}=5.6 \mathrm{~L}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What amount of $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ gas liberated at anode, if 1 ampere current is passed for 30 minute from NaCl solution?
questions.solution:
$2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \rightarrow \underset{1 \text { mole }}{\mathrm{Cl}_2}+\underset{2 \times 96500 \text { coulomb }}{2 e^{-} \text {(At anode) }}\begin{aligned} Q & =i t=1 \times 30 \times 60 \\ & =1800 \text { coulomb }\end{aligned}$
The amount of chlorine liberated by passing 1800 coulomb of electric charge
$=\frac{1 \times 1800 \times 71}{2 \times 96500}=0.66 \mathrm{~g}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How much chlorine will be liberated on passing one ampere current for 30 min through NaCl solution?
questions.solution:
According to Faraday's law
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{w}{E}=\frac{i t}{96500} \\ & \text { or } \quad \frac{w}{35.5}=\frac{1 \times 30 \times 60}{96500} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad=0.662 \mathrm{~g} \\ & \end{aligned}$
so, 0.662 g chlorine is liberated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two metals 'A' and 'B' have $\mathrm{E}_{\text {red }}^{\circ}$ value equal to 0.36 V and 1.23 V . What will be the correct cell equation?
questions.solution:
From $E_{\text {red }}^{\circ}$. values, it is clear that $A$ is more electropositive than $B$ (as it has lesser $E^{\circ}{ }_{\text {red }}$ ), hence it can replace $B$ from its salt solution and act as anode in galvanic cell. Hence, correct cell equation will be:
$A+B^{2+} \longrightarrow A^{2+}+B$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}\left(\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}, \mathrm{Zn}\right)=-0.763 \mathrm{~V}$ and $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}\left(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}, \mathrm{Fe}\right)=-0.44 \mathrm{~V}$, then the emf of the cell $\mathrm{Zn}\left|\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(\mathrm{a}=0.00 \mathrm{l}) \| \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}(\mathrm{a}=0.005)\right| \mathrm{Fe}$ is
questions.solution:
The cell reaction is
$\mathrm{Zn}+\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}+\mathrm{Fe}$
From Nernst equation
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{E}_{\text {cell }}=\mathrm{E}_{\text {cell }}^{\circ}-\frac{0.0591}{\mathrm{n}} \log \frac{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}}}{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}}} \\ & =(0.763-0.44)-\frac{0.0591}{1} \log \frac{0.001}{0.005} \\ & =0.364 \mathrm{~V} \\ & \end{aligned}$

options: tin is more reactive than iron
tin is less reactive than iron
reactivity of tin and iron is same
tin is oxidising agent while iron is not so

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the cell reaction
$\mathrm{Pb}+\mathrm{Sn}^{2+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Pb}^{2+}+\mathrm{Sn}$
Given that, $\mathrm{Pb} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Pb}^{2+}, E^{\circ}=0.13 \mathrm{~V}\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}+2 e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Sn} ; E^{\circ}=-0.14 \mathrm{~V}$
What would be the ratio of cation concentration for which $E=O$ ?
questions.solution:
For the given cell reaction,
$E_{\text {cell }}^{\circ}=-0.14 \mathrm{~V}+0.13 \mathrm{~V}=-0.01 \mathrm{~V}$
According to Nerst equation,
$\begin{aligned} E_{\text {cell }} & =E_{\text {cell }}^{\circ}-\frac{0.0591}{2} \log \frac{\left[\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\right]} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0 & =-0.01=\frac{0.0591}{2} \log \frac{\left[\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\right]}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \log \frac{\left[\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\right]}=\frac{0.01}{-0.0296}=-0.3 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\left[\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\right]}=\operatorname{antilog}(-0.3) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\left[\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\right]}=0.5 \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statement is not correct about an inert electrode in a cell?
options: It does not participate in the cell reaction.
It provides surface either for oxidation or for reduction reaction.
It provides surface for conduction of electrons.
It provides surface for redox reaction
questions.solution: Inert electrodes provide surface for oxidation or reduction reaction but not for redox reaction. Hence, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of moles of oxygen obtained by the electrolytic decomposition of 108 g water is
questions.solution:
\(\begin{array}{ll}
2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \xrightarrow{\text { Electrolysis }} 2 \mathrm{H}_2+ &\mathrm{O}_2 \\
2 \text{mol} & 1 \text{mol} \\
2 \times 18 =36 g
\end{array}\)
\(\because 36 \mathrm{~g}\) of \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\) produce 1 mole of oxygen
\(\therefore 108 \mathrm{~g}\) of water will produce oxygen
\(=\frac{108}{36}=3 \mathrm{~mol}\)
